instruction: Basic single-room building shell. Open `/opt/blender/blender` first; Bonsai is available inside it as the installed BIM extension. Open the provided /home/user/Desktop/init.ifc IFC4 model in Bonsai and use it as the starting project. The provided file is an editable metric IFC4 single-room building shell with placeholder space names and an unfinished window set. In Bonsai/Blender, rename the spaces to the required room names and add the required window objects, then save the only required deliverable on the Desktop as /home/user/Desktop/result.ifc using Bonsai's IFC save/export controls. The final model must contain one rectangular single-storey room about 5 m by 4 m with four exterior walls about 3 m high, one floor slab, one real space, one door, and one window. The space must be named Room 101 so it exports as an IfcSpace. The deliverable must contain real IFC/BIM elements for the required wall, slab, door, window, and space objects rather than ordinary Blender mesh placeholders or visual-only geometry. The exported IFC should use the IFC4 schema, have unique GlobalId values for IfcRoot objects, and contain at least one IfcProject, one IfcSite, one IfcBuilding, one IfcBuildingStorey, one IfcSpace named Room 101, four wall-like IfcWall or IfcWallStandardCase elements, one IfcSlab, one IfcDoor, and one IfcWindow. The shaped model should have an overall size roughly matching the single-room shell, with X span about 5 m, Y span about 4 m, and Z span about 3 m. Other coordinates, wall thicknesses, opening positions, materials, object type names, relationship nesting, property sets, and harmless exporter metadata may vary as long as the saved IFC satisfies these requirements.
